sections.h2: Where a Miami County deed is recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Miami County property are recorded at the Recorder's Office, 201 West Main Street, Troy, OH 45373. Call (937) 440-6040, or fax (937) 440-6034. The office is open weekdays from 8 am until 4 pm. More detail is on the county's recorder page.

The Recorder keeps the permanent chain of title: deeds, mortgages, easements, leases, plats and veteran discharges. Valuation and tax collection sit elsewhere. The Auditor sets values and assessments, the Treasurer collects taxes and the Clerk of Courts handles property disputes. The office handles 15,169 documents a year, including 6,259 deeds and 4,319 mortgages, and 9,806 of the total come in electronically.

Pages one and two together cost $39.00, then $8.00 for every page added, as the documents and fees page shows. A $5.00 preservation fee is built into that price, and part of each fee goes to the state's housing trust fund under sections 317.32 and 317.36.

Miami County sample recording fees, effective January 1, 2025
Document lengthRecording fee
1 or 2 pages$39.00
3 pages$47.00
4 pages$55.00
6 pages$71.00
10 pages$103.00

Other charges that can land on a sale or a payoff:

  • A $4.00 marginal notation fee on mortgage releases, assignments and modifications.
  • A $20.00 fee when a document breaks the Ohio standardization guidelines.
  • No fee to record or copy a military discharge (DD-214).

If you mail the original, enclose a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself.

A deed must clear the County Engineer and the Auditor first. Under the conveyance standards adopted August 12, 2025, every instrument is approved for transfer by the Engineer's Office, with a signed DTE 100 value statement or a DTE 100EX exemption form turned in alongside it.

Three rules in those standards matter to sellers:

  • No transfer is approved when the grantor never appears as an earlier grantee, unless the deed or an affidavit under section 5301.252 explains the gap in the chain of title.
  • A deed that carves a piece off an existing parcel, or changes the legal description, needs a boundary survey plat that the Engineer reviews.
  • Anyone claiming an exemption must prove it to the Auditor. If doubt remains, the fee is charged or the parcel does not transfer.

The Auditor's fee comes from section 319.54: $1, or ten cents per $100 of value if that is larger. Separately, section 322.02 lets county commissioners levy a transfer tax that tops out at 30 cents on each $100. Sellers pay both. Call the Miami County Auditor to learn which applies before you build a closing statement.

Deeds are one entry on a long list. The Recorder also accepts affidavits, easements, land contracts, leases, mechanic's liens, notices of commencement, powers of attorney, sheriff's deeds, survivorship deeds, trust documents and warranty deeds. A few carry their own prices:

  • Federal tax lien: $5.00 to file and $3.00 to release.
  • Release of a personal property tax lien: $4.00.
  • Financing statement: $12, plus $4 for each name indexed.
  • Living will or durable power of attorney for health care: $28 minimum, $40 maximum.
  • Plats: ten cents a square inch, minimum $40.00.
  • Faxed pages: $2 local or toll-free, $4 long distance.

Sellers most often meet the mortgage release. If a lender never recorded one after an old payoff, the lien still shows on the record, so ask the title agent to check before the buyer's lender does.

sections.h2: What the value statement asks the seller
sections.html:
The buyer's statement under section 319.202 records whether the seller expects a reduced tax bill, such as the homestead or owner-occupancy credit, and whether the land was enrolled in the agricultural use valuation. A yes on either needs a sworn paper that both sides have accounted for the amount.

Farm ground deserves a question. If a seller's acreage was enrolled, leaving the program can trigger a recoupment charge, and the buyer and seller are expected to account for it before the Auditor endorses the deed.

For a rental, the Auditor's stamp also reminds the buyer to file landlord information with the Auditor under section 5323.02.

sections.h2: Looking up and copying land records
sections.html:
The county's records search page offers a free basic search by last and first name, or business name, in the AVA database. Images carry a watermark, and a watermarked copy is not accepted for recording.

  • Basic search: free to view and print, with a watermark.
  • Clean copies: email or call the Recorder's Office. Since January 2026 copies cost $2.00 per page, paid in advance.
  • Credit cards: a service fee of $2.00 or 2.65% applies, whichever is greater. Cash and check are also taken.
  • Title searchers: Laredo Anywhere, run by Fidlar Technology, reaches deeds back to the county's start in 1807.

Deeds from 1807 through 1979 are scanned as whole books. Records for 1980 through 2008 are only partly indexed, and for anything before 1980 you should contact the office. A certified copy is $2.00 a page, and each seal adds $1.00.

sections.h2: Can a title company e-record a deed?
sections.html:
E-recording suits businesses that file regularly, not one-time submissions. The e-recording page lists five vendors: ePN, Simplifile, Hopdox, Indecomm and CSC. Each sets its own pricing, so a title agent signs up with a vendor directly.

A private seller closing without a title company can send the deed by mail or hand it over at the window. Ask the Recorder's Office at (937) 440-6040 whether your document type can go electronically before you plan around it.

Troy is the county seat, and the county's cities are Troy, Piqua and Tipp City, plus slices of Huber Heights and Union. The 2025 headcount is 112,634, a 3.5% gain on the 2020 base, spread over 47,930 housing units. Roughly three in four homes are lived in by their owners (73.4%). Median home value stands at $229,100 and median household income at $76,817. The county issued 340 building permits in 2025.

A sale of any kind, from a tidy listing to a tenant-occupied fixer, follows one path here: Engineer, Auditor, Recorder. For a cash sale the lender's paperwork disappears, but those three stops stay. Start the Engineer's review early if the legal description needs any change, because a survey plat adds time.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Miami County Recorder?
faqs.a: The office sits at 201 West Main Street in Troy, OH 45373. Call (937) 440-6040; it is open weekdays from 8 am until 4 pm.

faqs.q: What is the Miami County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: Two pages cost $39.00, which includes a $5.00 preservation fee, and every extra page adds $8.00. A $4.00 marginal notation fee applies to mortgage releases, assignments and modifications, and a $20.00 fee applies when a document misses the Ohio standardization rules.

faqs.q: Who covers the conveyance fee when a Miami County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller settles it with the Auditor before recording. State law sets the minimum at $1, rising to ten cents per $100 on larger values, and a local transfer tax may be added if the commissioners adopted one. The Auditor can tell you what applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: Does Miami County need a survey to split a parcel?
faqs.a: Yes. A boundary survey plat is required when a deed cuts up an existing parcel or changes its legal description, and the County Engineer reviews it before the Auditor accepts the deed.

faqs.q: Can I print my deed for free in Miami County?
faqs.a: Yes. Anyone can pull up and print a watermarked image through the basic records search without paying. A copy without the watermark must be requested from the Recorder's Office and costs $2.00 per page.
